rows.R: Results say the lower CI limit (-1.64%) 'was greater than the threshold' (-1%), yet -1.64 < -1.00. The rule (lower limit must exceed -1%) and the conclusion (noninferiority not shown) are correct; only the direction word is wrong. Wald recomputation of 44/1018 vs 43/1022 gives a lower limit of -1.64.
rows.evidence: Main article jama_jabre_2018_oi_180004.pdf PDF p.3 (Statistical Analysis: NI rule) and p.4 (Primary Outcome paragraph).
rows.rationale: Read both passages. Rule p.3: noninferiority accepted if the lower CI limit is higher than -1%. p.4: difference 0.11% (1-sided 97.5% CI -1.64% to infinity), 'The lower limit ... was greater than the threshold of noninferiority, thus noninferiority was not demonstrated.' -1.64 < -1.00, so 'greater' is wrong; it should read lower. Recomputed Wald interval for 44/1018 vs 43/1022: difference 0.115 points, lower limit -1.64, matching the printed value. The conclusion is consistent with the numbers, so the interpretation is unaffected. Confirmed, minor wording error.

The operator difference (>= vs >) is real, and the combination rule also differs between plan (and) and report (or). Exactly 60 mL/kg is a common cumulative volume with 20 mL/kg boluses, so classification of the main secondary outcome could differ. Which rule was applied is not documented. Retained as a substantive planned-versus-reported definition difference; agree with AI domain.

Counts are arithmetically coherent under this valid outcome-specific rule. Not explicitly stated by the authors, but a satisfactory explanation, so excluded per the Codebook.

rows.R: Original protocol p.16 says the primary outcome is 'the child's BMI Percentile' and 'change of BMI%', but its table gives weight (kg)/height (m2), and the original SAP section of the same protocol (p.37-38), the DSMB-approved SAP (p.108), the revised protocol (p.67) and the final SAP all model raw BMI, as reported. The label looks loose rather than a changed outcome.

rows.rationale: Read p.16 and searched the bundle for 'percentile' and 'BMI%': the only primary-outcome use of percentile is p.16. Every planned analysis specification models BMI (kg/m2) trajectory, matching the report (e.g., eTable 1 means of 16.7-17.8). BMI percentile and raw BMI are different metrics for children, so the label is not trivial, but the operational plan is consistently raw BMI. Rated minor_presentation because the conflict is in labeling, not in the analysis actually planned.

rows.R: Control (GROW Smarter) exposure: original protocol = 12 quarterly 60-min sessions over 3 years; revised protocol = a 45-min school-readiness program at each of 7 data-collection points plus a quarterly newsletter; article = six 30-min group activities concurrent with data collection. The original-to-revised change reflects a protocol revision; the report vs revised (30 vs 45 min) is unexplained.
rows.evidence: Protocol/SAP bundle joi180075supp1_prod.pdf PDF p.14 (original protocol), p.64 (revised protocol), p.106-107 (amendment summary; no entry on control-session dose found); Main article jama_barkin_2018_oi_180075.pdf PDF p.1 and p.3.
rows.rationale: Verified the three descriptions. 12 x 60 = 720 min; 7 x 45 = 315 min (6 x 45 = 270 within 36 months); 6 x 30 = 180 min. The amendment summary I checked records the arm renaming but no change in control-session length. The described control dose differs between the latest plan and the report. Because both arms received the school-readiness program, the discrepancy does not alter the between-arm contrast as described, but the reported control-condition dose does not match the latest plan. Recorded as a substantive procedural difference in description, without inferring an unjustified change.

rows.R: Figure 1 (CONSORT) gives 282 children with BMI measured at 9 mo (control); Figure 2 and eTable 1 give 280 at the same visit (2 fewer). The flow note defines the number as children for whom BMI was collected. An unexplained, small difference that recurs across visits; it does not affect the ITT mixed model (all 304/306 analyzed).

rows.rationale: Read the rendered Figure 1 and Figure 2 and the eTable 1 text. Control 9 mo: 282 vs 280; difference 2. Flow arithmetic is internally consistent (e.g., intervention 3 mo 288+9+7 = 304; control 3 mo 277+25+4 = 306; all visits close to 304/306). Figure 2 and eTable 1 agree with each other and give smaller counts at every visit except control 36 mo (272 in both), and the baseline counts in Figure 2 (298/302) are also below 304/306, which suggests the box plots and eTable use a cleaned or within-window subset whose exclusion rule is not reported. A real count inconsistency between report displays; minor because the differences are 1-9 children, the descriptive tables are internally consistent, and the primary model uses all randomized children.
